articles.title: India's First -Ever Kunafa Stick Is In Hyderabad With Unreal Cheese Pull! | Curly Tales
articles.content: Home / India / Food / India’s First-Ever Kunafa Stick Is In Hyderabad With Unreal Cheese Pull! An element of convenience, cheesy pull and a little performance give Kunafa Stick the potential to become the next viral dessert in India. by Sannjanaa Shenoyy Updated: August 29, 2026 2:09 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Instagram/ @nomme.hyd Straight from the Middle East, Kunafa is slowly finding a loyal fan base amongst Indian foodies. The textured crunch from the shredded kataifi dough, gooey cheesy filling and sweetness from the sugar syrup make it a nuanced dessert. Traditionally, it’s savoured as a sit-down dish with a fork and spoon. But if Sushi could get a grab-and-go twist, then why not Kunafa? Hyderabad just introduced India to its first-ever Kunafa Stick; let’s tell you where you can grab one. Kunafa Stick Arrives In Hyderabad View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nomme (@nomme.hyd) Hyderabad-based NOMME and Gourmet Baklava have changed the dessert game. Live counters at these stores let guests watch their shredded pastry dough on sticks being deep-fried in ghee, dunked in sugar syrup and then drizzled with playful sauces of pistachio, Lotus Biscoff , Nutella or all three. It’s like theatre for desserts. An element of convenience, cheesy pull and a little performance give Kunafa Stick the potential to become the next viral dessert in India. The handheld version of the Middle Eastern dessert is a pretty phyllo dough cylinder, with a stringy cheesy pull, finished with sugar syrup and sauces. Kunafa is a rich dessert with indulgent notes. Also Read: Ever Tried Kunafa Popsicles? Papa Kanafa Offers 15+ Kunafa Options That Will Leave You Drooling Grab-And-Go Variant Has Roots In Jordan While it’s a delight to sit around the table and crack a Kunafa together, the grab-and-go variant has a touch of playfulness. Watch your Kunafa being prepared meticulously at Nomme or Gourmet Baklava at the live counter. Select a sauce to go with it, then walk around with your Kunafa Stick, without needing a spoon or a plate. At first glance, it looks like a Korean Corn Dog. But that’s the beauty of it. Whether it’s Sushi Push Pop or a Corn Dog, these are snackables that are easier to enjoy. Interestingly, the Kunafa Stick is not a culinary invention. Rather, it’s a classic from Jordan that has now made its way to Hyderabad. Also Read: Pistachio Kunafa Croissant & Doughnuts Are Flying Off The Shelves; Here’s Where You Can Try Them So, when are you planning to try the soon-to-be viral Kunafa Stick in Hyderabad? Deets Where: NOMME Coffee Theatre, Banjara Hills Road No. 2, opposite KBR Park When: 12:30 pm to 1 am (Weekdays) and 12 pm to 1 am (Weekends) Where : Gourmet Baklava, Banjara Hills Road No. 3 and Sarath City Capital Mall When: 10 am to 12:30 am Cost: ₹249 onwards FAQs What is a Kunafa Stick? Kunafa Stick is a playful grab-and-go Jordanian twist given to the dish originating in the Middle East....

articles.title: Meet 'Samarthak': India's First Indigenously Built Multi-Purpose Naval Support Vessel
articles.content: In an important development for India's maritime defense capabilities, the Indian Navy has received its first two Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPVs) built with the help of indigenous technology and resources. The vessel is built by a leading private shipbuilding company named Larsen & Toubro (L&T) at its Kattupalli Shipyard at Chennai and represents an achievement in India's defense manufacturing system due to the implementation of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat policy by the current government in India. The vessel is named Samarthak meaning "The Supporter," and has around 75% local content in its design and building. Unlike the traditional combat vessels designed for a single mission, this new-generation vessel is designed to be a flexible auxiliary ship with many different applications which include live armament testing, target towing, maritime surveillance and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Operations (HADR) in the Indian Ocean Region. Technical Specifications Samarthak has been constructed to ensure high durability, stability, and multi-functionality. The main specifications of the ship are as follows: Displacement: About 3750 tonnes Length: 107 m Beam: 18.6 m Maximum Speed: 15 knots Operational range: 4500 nautical miles Personnel capacity: 116 personnel (with 8 officers included) Producer: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) Shipbuilding, Kattupalli Indigenous content: More than 75% Multi-functional Capabilities and Applications The idea of the Multi-purpose Vessel class is operational flexibility. By performing non-combat supporting missions, Samarthak allows the use of surface combatants for their primary deterrent and combat tasks. Testing Platform for Developmental Weaponry: The ship becomes a real-life marine test facility. This allows DRDO and other domestic defense companies to test, tune and verify defense sensors, sonar, radar, and weapons before they go to the front lines. Training Platform for Fleet Gunnery and ASW The ship has equipment for launching High-Speed Surface and Air Targets and carrying out torpedo launch and recovery operations during fleet air defense and ASW exercises. Mother Ship for the Unmanned Systems After being designed specifically for network-centric warfare, the ship can deploy, control and recover unmanned systems, such as UAVs, USVs, and underwater systems. Service Ship for Maritime Patrol Operations and Regional Surveillance Service The ship will be responsible for offshore patrol operations, surveillance, and monitoring of coastal zones to protect vital shipping lines. HADR and Environmental Response This advanced platform comes with on-board medical facilities, space to carry out relief operations, crane lifting equipment, and ocean towing devices. It also has equipment to handle marine pollution control. The introduction of Samarthak can be seen as a move towards encouraging public-private partnerships in manufacturing of defense equipment. According to the agreement made between MoD and L&T in March 2022 and two MPVs were ordered. Utkarsh, the second vessel of this type has been launched and is undergoing trials at sea before being officially handed over.

articles.title: Suzuki Motorcycle India inaugurates India's first 'Suzuki Lounge' in Thane - Chennai Patrika
articles.content: Suzuki Motorcycle India Pvt. Ltd. (SMIPL), the two-wheeler subsidiary of Suzuki Motor Corporation, Japan, today inaugurated India’s first ‘ Suzuki Lounge’ – a new integrated service and customer experience outlet designed to make workshop visits more comfortable, transparent and engaging. SMIPL’s first Suzuki Lounge, Riddhi Auto Agencies LLP (Riddhi Suzuki) in Pimpalghar, Bhiwandi, Thane (Maharashtra) , was inaugurated by Mr. Vivek Jain (Assistant Vice-President - After Sales, SMIPL). and Mr. Osamu Tani (Operation Manager - After Sales, SMIPL) in the presence of officials from SMIPL and Riddhi Suzuki. Commenting on the inauguration, Mr. Hari Krishna K., Executive Officer, Sales & After-Sales, Suzuki Motorcycle India Pvt. Ltd ., said, “Suzuki Lounge represents a significant step forward in our customer-centric approach and brings the spirit of ‘By Your Side’ into the service experience. Today’s customers expect more than just service. They seek transparency, comfort, and a premium experience. With Suzuki Lounge, we are creating an environment where customers can relax, stay connected, and confidently witness the care and expertise that goes into servicing their vehicles.” Suzuki Lounge: Where Service Meets Customer Experience Suzuki Lounge brings together a modern service workshop, premium customer lounge and dedicated new vehicle display area within a thoughtfully designed environment, offering customers more than a conventional workshop visit. The customer lounge reflects a hospitality-led approach , with contemporary interiors, warm wooden accents and soft, well-balanced lighting. A café-style reception , comfortable seating and dedicated discussion spaces create a welcoming setting for customers during their service visit. The service area remains visually connected to the lounge through an open layout and glass partitions , providing customers clear visibility of workshop activities while trained Suzuki technicians attend to their vehicles. The Thane outlet is equipped with four service bays. Complementing the service and lounge areas is a dedicated new vehicle display zone , where customers can explore Suzuki’s latest motorcycles and scooters and learn more about their features during their visit. By combining hospitality-inspired spaces with greater openness around the service process and opportunities for product discovery, Suzuki Lounge creates a more reassuring and engaging customer experience. With the introduction of Suzuki Lounge, SMIPL is further strengthening its after-sales network and customer touchpoints , while bringing a more contemporary approach to the service journey. articles.content: Support our Journalism 9th Anniversary: Free Tote & Mug Subscribe Home India Education Amaravati to get India’s first dedicated university for quantum tech, AI and... Education Tech Amaravati to get India’s first dedicated university for quantum tech, AI and other deep-tech fields Andhra Pradesh has approved Rs 730-cr NIELIT-led university in Amaravati focused on quantum computing, AI, semiconductors, other emerging technologies, with 8,250 learners to be trained over 5 years. Deepika Amirapu 29 August, 2026 09:44 am IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu announcing India’s first dedicated Quantum and Artificial Intelligence University campus in Amaravati | X Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Hyderabad: Andhra Pradesh is set to become the focal point for India’s next-generation deep tech ecosystem, with the state granting its approval for India’s first dedicated Quantum and Artificial Intelligence University campus in Amaravati. Spearheaded by the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), the university will be fully funded by the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). At Rs 730 crore, the 8.5-acre campus will be built in the Capital Region Development Authority (CRDA), and the initiative is expected to bridge the global deep-tech industry’s demands, officials in Andhra Pradesh said. The CM decided to establish the university at the CRDA Authority meeting, which he chaired with other officials at the state secretariat Thursday, according to the official statement. Show Full Article This institutional milestone could hold multifaceted significance for regional governance, industry development, and student career trajectories in the state as the campus will host dedicated Centres of Excellence (CoEs) and startup co-working spaces. The CoE would also collaborate with premier institutions like IIT Tirupati and IIIT Sri City, a government press release read. The origin of this deep-tech university was outlined in the Quantum Tech policy that was launched in November 2025 in Amaravati. Called the Amaravati Quantum Valley Declaration, Andhra released its five-year Quantum Computing Policy, following which Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu laid the physical foundation stone for the Amaravati Quantum Valley project in February 2026. Shortly after, on 14 April 2026 (World Quantum Day), the state inaugurated India’s first open-access Quantum Reference Facilities. Minister for IT, RTGS, and HRD Nara Lokesh, said on X at the time, “From vision to qubits, Andhra Pradesh is building India’s quantum future. India’s first indigenous, open-access quantum computers are here, marking the rise of Amaravati Quantum Valley as a global hub. The future is here, in Amaravati—built in India, open to India, for the world.” The new university will focus on quantum technologies, artificial intelligence, semiconductors and other emerging deep-tech areas, integrating education, research, skilling, innovation and entrepreneurship, the release detailed. Until the campus is built, the academic and skill-development programmes will be conducted at existing facilities in the Acharya Nagarjuna University in Guntur. “NIELIT is a Deemed-to-be University (Distinct Category) under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956 and the UGC Regulations, 2023. articles.title: Karnataka FDA cancels India's first 'Peptide Party' in Koramangala - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | Karnataka FDA cancels India’s first biohacking ‘Peptide Party’ in Koramangala India’s inaugural biohacking event, the ‘Peptide Party’, was cancelled before it commenced on August 29 in Koramangala, Bengaluru. The event, organised by Peptide OS and Offlyn Life and limited to 50 guests, was designed as a networking salon for wellness enthusiasts, influencers and biohackers. The party featured discussions on physical optimisation and longevity, alongside an experimental menu offering “peptide mocktails” — beverages infused with short-chain amino acid compounds claimed to aid cell repair, fat loss, muscle growth and anti-ageing. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google Following its promotion on social media, the event received swift criticism from medical professionals and clinical researchers. They raised ethical and legal concerns about providing unverified, research-grade signalling molecules in an unsupervised setting. Experts also highlighted the unpredictable bioavailability and efficacy of peptides delivered via drinks or oral solutions, warning against the use of unverified synthetic compounds. Amid growing public scrutiny, the Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration intervened. The regulator issued inquiries and notices to the organisers, requesting detailed information on the chemical composition of the proposed peptide mocktails, the sourcing of the active ingredients, and whether the venue was authorised to serve unapproved biological agents as food or beverage additives. ADVERTISEMENT Consequently, the event was officially cancelled, preventing it from proceeding as planned. Written by TNM (With ANI Inputs) This story is written by TNM Bureau with inputs from ANI. articles.title: Pune police and Military Intelligence detain three Bangladeshi nationals over illegal stay
articles.content: ANI Photo | Pune police and Military Intelligence detain three Bangladeshi nationals over illegal stay Pune City Police’s Special Branch, in collaboration with Military Intelligence, detained three Bangladeshi nationals allegedly residing illegally in the city on August 27, officials said. The individuals have been identified as Sonia Akther, Motiar Gaji and Sonia Moti Pan. Acting on specific intelligence input, a joint operation was conducted around 3 pm resulting in their detention. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google During preliminary questioning and verification, authorities discovered the trio were residing in India without valid documentation. Detention orders are being issued, and they will remain in custody pending further legal proceedings and deportation formalities. The operation is part of intensified surveillance by intelligence and law enforcement agencies in Pune aimed at identifying persons without valid documents and uncovering networks involved in illegal entry or residence. ADVERTISEMENT Separately, Pune City Police announced a complete ban on plasma sound systems and pressure mids ahead of the upcoming festive season, including Dahi Handi and Ganeshotsav. Violators will face seizure of sound equipment and legal action under the Noise Pollution Rules. Pune City Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar reported that six high-decibel sound setups were seized during recent Eid processions as enforcement against noise pollution was intensified ahead of the festivals. The police are discussing proposals with political leaders, dahi handi organisers and Ganesh mandals to limit procession sound systems to a maximum of “4 Base + 4 Top” speakers. While reasonable limits on sound usage are being considered, there will be zero tolerance for unapproved high-decibel equipment generating uncontrolled noise. ADVERTISEMENT “A total of 100% mutual consensus has been reached that any kind of plasma and pressure mid, through which uncontrolled noise is generated, has been completely banned,” Mr Kumar said. “All Ganesh mandals have assured us of voluntary compliance. If there is any violation of this anywhere, legal action under the Noise Pollution Rules will be taken, and the sound system will be seized.” Written by TNM (With ANI Inputs) This story is written by TNM Bureau with inputs from ANI.
